Thanks for the product overview yesterday. We want to make sure the implementation plan maps to the model and context choices so our latency-sensitive traces (customer chat + automated summaries) stay within budget. A few quick facts on our side: 

- Typical session length: 2–4 user messages plus system prompt (avg 650 tokens total per session).
- Peak concurrent sessions expected during business hours: ~45–60.
- Daily active users (first 90 days): ~2,500 with 1.2 sessions/day on average.
- We send a historical context window of up to 8k tokens for high-touch accounts, but can trim to 3k for lower tiers.

Questions: can you propose a shortlist of model variants (including a quantized option) and a token-volume estimate that ties into Redwood Dedicated sizing? Also any quick wins on prefix/KV caching for repeated account context would be great.

I attached a simple token profile export from our prototype.

Thanks Aditya — did a quick pass on sizing with the attached assumptions. High level notes: 

- Workload assumptions (from Maria + conservative buffers): avg session 700 tokens, 60 concurrent at peak, 2,500 DAU -> ~1,750 sessions/day.
- Token estimate (peak hour): assuming 60 concurrent sessions * 700 tokens in 1 hour -> 42k tokens/hour; scaled to sustained peak (8-hour window) -> ~336k tokens/day at peak.
- Model shortlist suggestion (production / fallback):
  1) redwood-compat-7b-v2 (FP16) — production: good balance of latency and quality for dialogue + summarization.
  2) redwood-compat-7b-q4_0 (int8/quant) — fallback for burst/low-cost path with ~1.8x throughput improvement in our tests.
  3) redwood-compat-13b-v1 (FP16) — reserved for high-quality summaries for enterprise accounts (scheduled batch ops).

- Autoscaling note: plan for base Dedicated pool sized to handle 60 concurrent low-latency sessions on 7b FP16 with a 20% headroom; burst to quantized nodes for spikes.
- Caching: prefix caching of static customer metadata and KV cache for the last two assistant turns should cut token spend by ~12–20% for repeated flows.

I'll attach a quick spreadsheet with estimated GPU hours and recommended Dedicated SKU mix. If this looks ok, we can convert to MAP numbers.

Rishi
